messages:
oliver: Quick follow-up from the SDK surface convo earlier — we need a concrete migration + compatibility plan for pagination cursors and transport retries. TL;DR: propose a 3-phase grace period to move consumers off blocking sync cursors and toward streaming/async iterators and compact continuation tokens.

hana: +1. can you outline why we need to force this now? any breaking perf wins? :eyes:

oliver: Two big reasons: 1) transport-level retry semantics are simpler with opaque compact tokens (we can resume without re-running server-side stateful steps). 2) lang parity: TS/Python already have ergonomic async streams; Go's idiom leans channel-based streams — keeping a single sync iterator surface forces awkward shims and subtle idempotency bugs.

kevin: Also, on performance, compact tokens let us avoid large cursor blow-ups for long-running sessions (KV cache footprint drops). Seen in infra traces.

maggie: I want to see a migration path where consumers can opt-in gradually. No sudden removals.

oliver: Agreed. Proposed phases: 
1) Announcement + dual-support (0-3 months): accept both old resume-token v1 and new compact cursor v2; server returns both where possible; clients default to v1 but expose v2 opt-in flag.
2) Deprecation (3-9 months): client libraries emit deprecation warnings when v1 used; SDKs provide helpers to convert/resume; server-side telemetry marks heavy v1 users for outreach.
3) Sunset (9-12 months): stop returning v1 in new runs; emergency compatibility window for enterprise customers with Dedicated/Private.

hana: Sounds reasonable. How do retries behave across this? If we change token format, we must ensure idempotency guarantees are clear to SDK users.

oliver: Good point. Proposal for retry semantics: 
- For unary calls: same as today.
- For paginated/streamed calls using v1 (stateful resume): do not retry non-idempotent steps automatically; surface explicit `retryable_checkpoint()` hook.
- For compact v2 tokens: design tokens to be full resume handles (stateless for server), allow transparent retries on transport errors.

kevin: Can you show example code for py/ts/go migration? small snippet would help teams.

oliver: Sure. Python (old -> new):
```python
# old sync cursor style (legacy)
for page in client.list_items_sync(request):
    process(page)

# new async/streaming (preferred)
async for item in client.list_items_stream(request):
    process(item)

# transitional helper (sync wrapper over streaming)
for item in client.list_items_stream(request).to_sync():
    process(item)
```

oliver: TypeScript: 
```ts
// old: callback/paged
for await (const page of client.listItemsAsync(request)) {
  doThing(page)
}

// shim to support sync where absolutely needed
const iter = client.listItemsAsync(request);
const toSync = makeBlocking(iter); // experimental helper
for (const p of toSync) doThing(p);
```

oliver: Go: prefer channels and explicit context cancellation:
```go
ch := client.ListItemsStream(ctx, req)
for itm := range ch {
  process(itm)
}
```

maggie: Nice. For the conversion helpers, do we want to include `to_sync()`/`makeBlocking()` in GA SDKs or only in a separate compat package? My worry: shipping it in core encourages bad sync usage forever.

raj: My take: provide compat helpers in a separate module (e.g., redwood-compat) for 6-9 months, then remove. Also ensure they log deprecation warnings the first N times they're used per process.

hana: Telemetry plan? We need metrics to track usage of v1 vs v2 and number of compat helper calls.

oliver: Server will emit `cursor_version` in logs/metrics for all pageable endpoints. Client SDKs should emit anonymous telemetry on opt-in. For private/dedicated, we'll expose an admin API to list active v1 sessions.

kevin: Rollout plan for SDK changes: 
- Beta release of v2 tokens + new streaming surfaces in next minor.
- Compat package released alongside.
- Enable server-side dual-token support behind a flag (default on).

maggie: Governance: which teams approve the sunset? product + infra + security? Need to notify enterprise SAs.

oliver: Approvals: product (maggie) + infra (kevin) + security (hana) + customer-success for outreach. I'll draft an announcement doc after alignment here.

raj: One more tricky thing: retries at the transport layer (grpc/unary/http). For compact tokens, do we require the transport layer to be idempotency-aware (e.g., attach `x-resume-token` header vs body)? If header, proxies can route without touching body which is nice.

kevin: Header approach seems cleaner for proxies, but header size limits worry me. Compact token aims to be small (<2KB). If we encode binary as base64 it's fine but keep under 2KB by design.

hana: Security note: tokens must be HMACed and time-bound when used across regions. Private deployments may opt for HSM signing; we need an API surface to plug KMS.

oliver: Noted. We'll add token signing + expiry metadata in spec.

maggie: Can you add a short checklist for SDK implementers? I want engineering teams to have concrete tasks.

oliver: Checklist (short):
- add streaming/async surface for pageable endpoints
- accept both v1 and v2 on client/server; expose opt-in flag
- add compat package with `to_sync()` helpers and deprecation logs
- emit telemetry for cursor_version and compat usage
- ensure token HMAC + expiry config exposed in Private/Dedicated
- update docs + migration guide with code snippets

kevin: LGTM. timeline proposal? We said 0-3 beta, 3-9 deprecate, 9-12 sunset. Ship SDK beta within 6 weeks?

oliver: I can land the server feature flag + token format draft by EOW. SDK PRs (python/ts/go) in 6 weeks for beta releases. I'll open RFC follow-up PR with the spec and the announcement draft.

maggie: Please include a short sample email/template for enterprise outreach. We'll need it for SAs.

oliver: Will do.

release-bot: deploy queued: infra/telemetry/cursor-metrics -> canary (sha: a1b2c3) :rocket:

raj: Thanks all. If nobody objects, I'll mark this thread as the canonical migration plan and start drafting the RFC follow-up doc. :+1:

hana: no objections from me. go for it.

kevin: +1

maggie: +1, ping me on the draft doc for wording on enterprise messaging.

oliver: Thanks. I'll post the RFC follow-up link here when ready. :party_parrot:
